summary: Publish a TypeScript npm library from a pushed version tag with provenance and no stored token, through a rerunnable publish helper.
description: Publish a TypeScript library to npm when a v-prefixed version tag is pushed. The workflow checks the tag against package.json, runs the project's checks, packs the tarball once and publishes exactly that file through npm trusted publishing, so no token is stored. A release script rewrites every place the version lives, and the publish helper checks the registry first so a rerun skips what is already out. First publication, the Trusted Publisher setting and the two-factor setting stay with the package owner.
seoDescription: Tag-driven npm releases for TypeScript libraries: trusted publishing, provenance, a version-bump script and a safely rerunnable publish helper.

projectExamples.title: Published parsing library
projectExamples.description: Release a small TypeScript parsing library to npm from version tags. Implement the parser in the base library stack; the owner publishes the first version by hand.

projectExamples.title: Scoped utility package
projectExamples.description: Publish a scoped utility package under an npm organization the owner controls. Configure the Trusted Publisher on npm after the first release.

plain.whatItIs: Publishes a TypeScript package to npm, the JavaScript package registry, whenever a version label is pushed to GitHub, with no password or token saved anywhere.
goodAt: Publishing from GitHub without storing an npm token
Updating the version in every file at once before a release
Rerunning a failed release without publishing anything twice
notGoodAt: Packages with several platform builds; extend the publish script for those.
Python or Go libraries; use their own release add-ons.

release to npm with provenance and no stored token

caveats: Provenance needs a public GitHub repository, and the first version of a new package is published by hand.
